title: Key-Dependent Complexity of Quantum Multidimensional Linear Attacks
summary: Existing estimates average key-dependent squared correlations and capacity under a concentration assumption; determine attack complexity across keys without relying solely on that assumption.

formal_statement.body: For quantum multidimensional linear attacks, squared correlations and capacity may vary significantly with the key, while complexity estimates replace these key-dependent quantities by their averages under the assumption that they concentrate around their means. Determine the attack complexity as a function of the key-specific squared correlations and capacity without relying solely on that concentration assumption, and characterize how variation across keys changes the complexity.

scope.domain: Quantum multidimensional linear cryptanalysis of symmetric ciphers.
assumptions: Average-based estimates assume that squared correlations and capacity concentrate around their means.
parameters: Cryptographic key: indexes potentially varying attack complexity
Key-specific squared correlations: key-dependent inputs to the complexity analysis
Key-specific capacity: a key-dependent input to the complexity analysis
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine complexity from key-specific squared correlations and capacity, and characterize its variation across keys without relying solely on concentration around mean values.

citations.label: Quantum Speed-Up for Multidimensional (Zero Correlation) Linear Distinguishers

progress.summary: The paper notes that squared correlations and capacity can vary significantly by key but estimates them using averages under a concentration assumption. It identifies an in-depth analysis of key-dependent complexity as important future work.
citation_labels: Akinori Hosoyamada et al., Quantum Speed-Up for Multidimensional (Zero Correlation) Linear Distinguishers
